messages:
alice_support: Escalating a live case for AcmePayments — they report SSE streams dropping with partial outputs and then duplicate billing events on reconnect. Happening across their Web SDK and a curl-based repro. Seen about every 30-90s during long streams.

ben_sre: Can you paste the minimal repro and any proxy/ALB in front? Also need observed response headers.

alice_support: Repro from customer (redacted):
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-xl" \
| sed -n '1,200p'
```
Logs show: last SSE event chunk then TLS EOF in client logs. No server 5xx in our app logs. They included a tcpdump snippet: `RST from client` after ~32s of silence.

carol_eng: Do we have any ALB/nginx timeouts set to 30s? Our default ALB idle timeout is 60s, but internal proxies sometimes have 30s. Which front door is this customer routed through?

alice_support: They’re on hosted-us-west -> edge: aws-nginx-prod (we have config for that). Customer said they saw silence then connection closed ~32s after last chunk.

ben_sre: Two hypotheses: 1) upstream proxy is terminating because no data was sent within its idle timeout; 2) client-side TCP keepalive/backoff or browser-level heuristics dropping connection. We should check if our runtime sends periodic comment pings or any keepalive.

carol_eng: Runtime currently sends comment pings on long polls only when `keepalive: true` is configured; default for streaming endpoints is OFF to reduce noise. That might explain it. If proxy idle timeout < client/server app idle, connection can get killed.

emma_l4: From the customer trace (headers):
```
via: 1.1 aws-nginx-prod
x-env: hosted-us-west
connection: Keep-Alive
keep-alive: timeout=5, max=1000
```
So the proxy advertises very short keep-alive. Also saw `tcp_nodelay: on` in logs.

ben_sre: Interesting — `keep-alive: timeout=5` is the socket header between client and proxy, not the proxy to origin. But the `via` shows they hit aws-nginx-prod. We need to inspect proxy idle timeout between ALB -> origin and nginx -> upstream. If there's a 30s idle there, and our server is not emitting any bytes for 30s, it will cut.

alice_support: Customer also reported being billed twice for the same generated tokens after reconnect — they reconnect and server restarts generation from scratch.

carol_eng: For billing duplication we need to confirm idempotency key behavior on reconnect. Currently our streaming endpoints accept `Idempotency-Key` on initial POST, but for streaming SSE reconnects we require `Last-Event-ID` or explicit resume token to resume a partial session. If client reconnects without resume token, server starts a fresh generation (billing new tokens).

ben_sre: Repro plan: 1) reproduce using their curl + a proxy set to idle timeout 30s; 2) instrument server to enable comment pings at 20s; 3) reproduce with `Last-Event-ID` resume to validate duplicate billing mitigation.

alice_support: I ran a quick local repro with `socat` simulating a blunt proxy idle close at 32s. Confirmed the client sees EOF, and our server had sent last chunk ~4s earlier. No comment pings were sent.

carol_eng: Quick config fixes:
- Short term: enable server-side comment pings by default for hosted until proxy configs are aligned. That would send `:keepalive\n\n` every 25s (SSE comment), preventing proxy idle termination.
- Mid term: ensure ALB/nginx upstream idle timeouts >= 75s for streaming routes.
- Long term: implement server-side resume tokens so reconnects can reattach to an in-progress generation and avoid double-billing.

ben_sre: Also add telemetry to detect frequent reconnects per session: rule when >2 reconnects within 2 minutes flag as suspect and correlate with billing events.

emma_l4: Proposed immediate workaround for customer: 1) set client to send `Last-Event-ID` header upon reconnect (if their client supports it) and 2) in the short-term we can toggle `keepalive_comments=true` on their workspace so our runtime sends pings every 25s.

alice_support: Customer agreed to try `keepalive_comments=true`. They asked if TCP keepalive would help.

carol_eng: TCP keepalive helps at the OS level but many proxies terminate based on HTTP inactivity regardless of TCP probes. SSE comment pings (application-level) are the most reliable cross-proxy solution. Also note browsers may suppress background tab connections.

ben_sre: For the billing duplication: add guard at billing layer: if a new session starts within N seconds of a previously terminated session for same user + same model + identical prompt fingerprint, mark it as probable-duplicate and hold billing pending until session completion or manual review. Not ideal but reduces immediate customer impact.

alice_support: Action items:
1) carol_eng: flip feature flag to enable `keepalive_comments` for hosted for AcmePayments and monitor for 24h.
2) ben_sre: run upstream proxy timeout audit and propose config changes (ALB/nginx) for streaming paths.
3) eng-platform: create a short-term billing dedupe rule (hold-and-defer) for near-duplicate sessions.
4) support: send reproducible curl + socat script to SRE/ENG so they can repro locally.

carol_eng: I’ll open an internal PR with the config change to default keepalive comments for streaming routes and add a quick flag per workspace. Also adding a note in docs about `Last-Event-ID` resume and recommend clients use it.

sse-bot: Deploy succeeded: `keepalive-comments:toggle` -> prod (canary 5%) :rocket:

ben_sre: After canary, I'll reach out to AcmePayments to confirm stability. If reconnects stop and billing duplicates disappear we can push full rollout.

alice_support: Thanks all — will update the customer and close loop once we have 24h observations. :+1:
